key_insight: A Gaussian surface bump accelerates vortex-induced boundary-layer transition and three-dimensional development while preserving the spatio-temporal wave front characteristic of nonmodal instability.
engineering_relevance: Predicting transition under combined surface roughness and free-stream vortices requires accounting for rapid three-dimensional disturbance growth.
method: Perform 2D and 3D DNS of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations over a semi-infinite flat plate.
Combine a convecting vortex of fixed strength and sign with a Gaussian roughness bump.
Analyze instantaneous flow structures, vorticity dynamics, and nonlinear receptivity.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify four stages: roughness-generated disturbances, spatio-temporal amplification, wave-front emergence with unsteady separation bubbles, and bubble merging into turbulent spots.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative transition shifts, and findings for one Gaussian bump and fixed vortex forcing should not be generalized to arbitrary roughness or disturbances.
paper_title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Vortex-Induced Instability Over a Semi-Infinite Flat Plate with Discrete Roughness
